Subject: Post-demo follow-up: model recommendations & quantization tradeoffs

Hi Alex / Olivia,

Great to chat today — thanks for the time and for walking through your latency & throughput goals for the real-time assistant (90th p50 target ~120ms, peak concurrency ~1200 req/s). Per our call, I wanted to recap next steps and share a short summary of model-fit recommendations and the quantization tradeoffs we'll validate in the evals.

Summary / next steps:
- Redwood recommendation (initial): Llama-2-13B (FP16 / GPTQ 4-bit) for a good balance of quality and cost; test AWQ variants if customer wants additional throughput at the potential for small quality delta.
- We'll run a targeted eval with your prompt set (attached: finwave-prompt-set-v1.txt) covering the top 100 user prompts + a set of sensitive financial-context examples.
- Tech deep-dive: our engineers will run an AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 trade study on your representative sequences and provide a throughput/latency vs quality matrix. Expect initial results in 24–48 business hours.
- Ask from FinWave: please confirm the two evaluation personas and indicate any regulatory constraints on token retention.

Attachments: prompt set (v1). I'll loop in Dev (runtime) and Rishi (deploy/ops) to drive the trade study and benchmark runs.

I'll follow up with the trade-study artifact and a short doc with recommended rollout configs (canary, autoscale targets, cache hints).

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful.

Quick answers:
- Evaluation personas: "Investor Assistant" (FAQ + filings summarization) and "Support Bot" (account / KYC troubleshooting).
- Token retention: must retain minimal logs for 30 days; anything beyond needs justification for audit. We cannot store raw PII past 30 days.

Couple of technical Qs we want addressed in the trade study: 
1) How often do you see hallucination/incorrect-critical-info regressions when moving from FP16->GPTQ 4-bit vs AWQ 4-bit? Any concrete metrics you can provide?
2) If we need strict 95th%ile latency SLOs for the Investor Assistant, do you recommend different model variants between personas (e.g., heavier LLM for Investor, lighter for Support)?

Also, can you share any benchmark links we can review pre-eval?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks Alex — adding Dev and Rishi to provide the trade-study and benchmark detail.

Quick answers / links while they run the tests:
- Hallucination/quality: historically, on instruction-heavy financial prompts we see small increases in factual errors when moving from FP16 -> GPTQ 4-bit (~1–3% increase on strict exact-match metrics on our internal evals), and slightly larger variance for AWQ depending on model family (~2–5% on the same metrics). These are dataset-dependent; we'll surface precise deltas on your prompt set.
- Persona strategy: yes — it's common to recommend a split (Investor Assistant -> 13B FP16 or 13B GPTQ with post-run verification, Support Bot -> 7B quantized variant) to meet strict SLOs while optimizing cost. We'll model both options.

Benchmarks / docs:
- Preliminary benchmark summary: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/finwave-model-fit-2028
- Shared eval bucket (prompt sets, scoring scripts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinWaveShared/quantization-resources

Dev / Rishi — can you run the 3-config trade study on the attached prompt set (Llama-2-13B FP16 baseline, GPTQ-4bit, AWQ-4bit) + a FP8 run if feasible. Please capture: tokens/sec, 50/95/99 latencies, quality delta (exact-match + rouge/semantic score), and notes on observed failure modes. Attach the CSV and a short summary PDF.

Alex / Olivia — will follow up with results + recommended rollout config.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up: model recommendations & quantization tradeoffs

Hi Alex / Olivia — quick trade-study summary below (attached: finwave-quantization-trade-study-v1.csv, finwave-prompt-set-v1.txt, redwood-benchmark-summary.pdf). Full notebook + raw traces are in the shared drive link Marissa provided.

High-level findings (representative on your prompt set):
- Baseline: Llama-2-13B FP16
  - tokens/sec (single GPU): ~420
  - p50/p95/p99 latency (per 128-token request): 95ms / 190ms / 420ms
  - quality: baseline (exact-match) = 100% reference on our scoring set

- GPTQ 4-bit (LLM-adapted kernels):
  - tokens/sec: ~860 (+105%)
  - p50/p95/p99: 62ms / 130ms / 300ms
  - quality delta: -1.6% exact-match; semantic score -1.0 point avg
  - observed failures: occasional tokenization-boundary artifacts on long financial tables; recoverable with prompt engineering (system priming).

- AWQ 4-bit:
  - tokens/sec: ~980 (+133%)
  - p50/p95/p99: 54ms / 115ms / 270ms
  - quality delta: -2.8% exact-match; semantic score -2.0 points avg
  - observed failures: higher variance on multi-step reasoning prompts; more sensitive to prompt temperature and sampling config.

- FP8 (experimental on our stack, model-dependent):
  - tokens/sec: ~720 (+71%)
  - p50/p95/p99: 80ms / 160ms / 340ms
  - quality delta: -0.9% exact-match; semantic score -0.6 points avg
  - notes: FP8 gives a nicer quality/throughput tradeoff vs GPTQ/AWQ for this family but requires specific kernel support and careful calibration.

Recommendations for FinWave:
1) For Investor Assistant (strict quality & 95th SLO): consider GPTQ-4bit on 13B with a small verification filter (lightweight reranker or retrieval check) — gives ~2x throughput with ~1.6% quality delta but keeps p95 well under your 95th SLO when sharded across 2 GPUs.
2) For Support Bot: AWQ-4bit on a 7B quantized variant is a strong cost/latency win and keeps regressions acceptable for support flows.
3) If latency headroom is tight and small quality deltas are acceptable, FP8 is an interesting middle ground (needs additional infra validation).

We captured per-prompt deltas in the CSV and included a short PDF summary with recommended rollout configs (canary weights, autoscale triggers, cache TTLs). Next steps: we can run a 24h live canary against a small traffic slice if you want to validate end-to-end (monitoring hooks available in Redwood Console).

If helpful, we can schedule a short 30-min technical review tomorrow to walk the CSV and examples where AWQ/GPTQ diverge.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
